items.title: Breakfast
items.hours: Hotel breakfast restaurant (B1) posted as 7:00–9:30 AM on weekdays (7:00–10:00 weekends); Tue Dec 8 is a weekday.
highlights: Buffet per the hotel's own post: congee with side dishes, cold noodles, salads, fruit, bread and toast, hot vegetables, egg dishes, soup, coffee and tea.
Eggs from the hot counter are the easiest protein before a long transit day.
tips: Hotel checkout is 11:00 AM, so the 8:30 AM departure is your own schedule, not a hotel constraint.
Breakfast opens at 7:00, so a 7:00–7:45 sitting buys margin if you choose the 9:00 AM THSR (see the THSR item).
items.watch: Breakfast hours come from a 2024 hotel post; the hotel says special dates may differ and are announced at check-in. Confirm the time at the desk the night before.

items.title: Checkout → MRT to THSR Zuoying
items.hours: Red Line from R11 Kaohsiung Main Station toward Gangshan: first train 06:00 on workdays.
items.getThere: Walk ~500 m from the hotel (33 Jianguo 3rd Rd) to MRT R11 Kaohsiung Main Station (Exits 1–4; Exits 1–3 have lifts). Take the Red Line in the 'Up' direction (toward Gangshan) to R16 Zuoying, then Exit 1, signed 'THSR Zuoying Station'.
highlights: R16 Zuoying Exit 1 connects to THSR Zuoying; Exit 2 goes to TRA New Zuoying.
Both R11 and R16 have island platforms, so you don't need to switch platforms with luggage.
tips: Use the lift at R11 Exits 1–3 with suitcases; Exit 4 has only an up escalator.
Allow extra time at Zuoying to get from the MRT to the THSR gates and pick up tickets if you didn't buy them online.
items.watch: The KRTC fare and journey time for R11→R16 weren't verifiable on the operator's site, so plan your own buffer for the THSR departure you choose.

items.title: THSR: Zuoying → Taoyuan
items.cost: Adult one-way, Zuoying→Taoyuan: Standard reserved NT$1,330; Business NT$2,200; Non-reserved NT$1,290. Child/concession: NT$665 / NT$1,100 / NT$645.
items.getThere: THSR Zuoying (south terminus) to Taoyuan: about 1 h 34–36 min on the faster trains (0616, 0618, 0622), or 1 h 53 min on 0814.
highlights: Best fit for the plan is 0618 at 09:00 (arrives 10:36). The 0622 at 09:35 (arrives 11:09) also works.
Non-reserved seats are in cars 10–12 on trains 0616, 0618 and 0622.
tips: Book reserved seats now: the timetable for Dec 8 already shows on THSR's search page.
The 0814 shows Early Bird and student discounts but takes 19 minutes longer. Choose a faster train unless the saving matters.
items.watch: There is no 9:15 AM departure. If you take the 09:35, you reach T1 around 11:36, which still leaves margin before the 12:20 counter close. Your booked ticket is final.

sources.label: THSR Timetable and Fare Search (queried for 2026/12/08)

items.title: Taoyuan Airport MRT: THSR → TPE Terminal 1
items.hours: Midday A18→A12 commuter trains leave at :02, :17, :32 and :47 past each hour (for example 10:47→11:06 and 11:17→11:36).
items.getThere: Walk from the THSR Taoyuan concourse to Airport MRT A18 Taoyuan HSR Station. Take a commuter train (all stops) to A12 Airport Terminal 1, 19 minutes.
highlights: From 10:30 to about 17:00 only commuter trains serve A18 toward the airport. Express trains stop at A18 only at set peak times.
If you take THSR 0618 (arrives 10:36), catch the 10:47 and reach A12 at 11:06. With 0622 (arrives 11:09), catch the 11:17 and reach A12 at 11:36.
tips: Buy single-journey tokens at the machines or the information counter, or tap a stored-value card.
Express trains (purple line) skip A18, so board the commuter train shown on the A18 platform.
items.watch: The operator says its timetable is for reference only. Leave buffer for airport formalities: the airport advises reaching airline counters 2–3 hours before departure.

items.title: Check-in, Airside Lunch, Gate
items.hours: Cathay Pacific TPE T1 counters open 180 min before departure (10:20 for CX495) and close at exactly 60 min before (12:20). Self-service kiosks and bag drop close 70 min before (12:10).
items.getThere: Cathay Pacific check-in: Terminal 1, Counter 4. Self-service kiosks and bag drop at Counters 3/4.
highlights: T1 3F Departure Area (airside) food options with posted hours: Burger King 06:00–23:00, Guiji 06:00–22:00, Hómee RICE 05:00–23:00, COMEME 06:00–22:00, Gontran Cherrier bakery 06:00–20:00, L.E.A.F CAFÉ 24 h.
Burger King or a rice set from Hómee RICE are the quickest protein-heavy choices before the flight.
tips: Check in online before you leave Kaohsiung, then use self-service bag drop. It closes 10 minutes earlier than the staffed counters.
The airport homepage shows live T1 security wait times; it read 10 min when checked.
items.watch: Cathay says counters close at exactly 60 minutes before departure. Arriving after 12:10 rules out self-service bag drop.

items.title: Cathay Pacific CX495: Taipei → Hong Kong
highlights: The timetable allows 2 h 05 min, but the flight usually takes about 1 h 20 min (806 km). Recent flights often landed 25–35 min early, around 14:45–15:05.
All of the last 9 flights tracked arrived on time (none 15+ min late).
tips: An early arrival leaves more of the evening in Hong Kong. Plan on landing before 15:25 but don't rely on it.
Gate assignments change. On Nov 11 it left from TPE gate B6; check your boarding pass and the screens.
items.watch: The cabin type and meal in the app notes weren't independently verified here. Your booking and boarding pass take precedence.

sources.label: Airportia – CX495 schedule and history

items.title: Touchdown Hong Kong (HKG T1) → Immigration → Bags
items.getThere: Arrival sequence: Immigration Hall → Baggage Reclaim → Customs & Excise → Arrivals Hall. The Airport Express ticket counters and trains are reached from the Arrivals Hall.
highlights: Visitors need only a valid travel document at Immigration.
Eligible frequent visitors can pre-enrol for the e-Channel using the Immigration Department's 'Go Hong Kong' app.
tips: Have passports out before the Immigration Hall.
Declare any dutiable goods above the duty-free limits at Customs.
items.watch: e-Channel pre-enrolment is only for eligible frequent visitors. First-time visitors should expect the staffed counters.

sources.label: HKIA – Arrivals passenger guide

items.title: Airport Express to Kowloon → Sasa Inn
items.hours: Airport Express runs about every 10 min, 05:54–00:48 daily (24 min to Hong Kong Station; Kowloon is the stop before).
items.cost: Airport → Kowloon, adult: HK$115 single smart ticket or HK$105 Octopus (child HK$57.5 / HK$52.5).
items.getThere: Airport Express to Kowloon Station, then a taxi to Sasa Inn: Flat C1, 8/F, Block C, Tsim Sha Tsui Mansion (華源大廈), 87 Nathan Road, Tsim Sha Tsui. Hotel nearest exit: TST MTR Exit C2.
highlights: Sasa Inn is licensed as Hotel/Guesthouse H/6290 (tel 5125 0008). The address matches the one in the app.
The building's official English name is Tsim Sha Tsui Mansion. Show taxi drivers the Chinese address 彌敦道87號華源大廈C座8字樓.
tips: Paying with Octopus saves HK$10 per adult on this fare.
Use the Chinese address in the app's Show card for the taxi.
items.watch: The MTR website was down for maintenance during research, so the free Airport Express shuttle and Kowloon taxi-stand details couldn't be verified.

items.title: Tsim Sha Tsui Harbourfront Walk
items.hours: Promenade always open. The WinterFest TST light show runs 7–11 PM. A Symphony of Lights ended with its final show on Nov 18, 2026.
highlights: Avenue of Stars: a 400 m harbour promenade with plaques, handprints and statues of Bruce Lee, Jackie Chan and Anita Mui.
Next to it on the Hung Hom Bypass is the 250 m Sports Wall of Fame, with portraits of 40+ Hong Kong Olympic and Asian Games medallists.
At dusk the Hong Kong Island skyline lights up across the harbour.
tips: HKTB recommends dusk for the day-to-night transition, which fits the 5:15 PM start.
The TST Winter Wonderland show starts at 7 PM on the TST harbourfront — it has replaced A Symphony of Lights.

sources.label: HKTB – Avenue of Stars

items.title: Mak Man Kee Wonton Noodles — Jordan
items.hours: Daily 12:00 noon – 12:30 AM. Closed Tuen Ng, Mid-Autumn and Lunar New Year days 1–3, none of which fall on Dec 8.
items.getThere: G/F, 51 Parkes Street, Jordan (白加士街51號地下), at MTR Jordan Exit C2. Tel 2736 5561.
highlights: Started in 1958 as a dai pai dong. Known for handmade wonton noodles brought from Guangzhou by founder Mak Woon-chi. Michelin Bib Gourmand.
Kwun Chung Market and Bowring Street Market are a short walk away if you want more to eat.
tips: The official menu (2025) is posted only as images on mmk.hk; check it there or in the shop.
Arriving around 6:30 PM is ahead of the busiest dinner hour. The app's 15-minute queue rule still applies.
items.watch: Dish prices couldn't be verified as text from an official source.

items.title: Temple Street / Yau Ma Tei Night Walk
items.hours: Temple Street between Jordan Road and Kansu Street is closed to cars 2 PM – midnight. Most stalls set up around 4 PM; busiest after dark until about 10–11 PM.
highlights: Street food near the Temple Street archway: claypot rice, fish balls, siu mai, plus pepper cakes, spicy skewers, Turkish lamb and Pakistani dishes.
Impromptu Cantonese opera performances and fortune-teller stalls.
Photo stops: the archway, Tin Hau Temple at Yau Ma Tei, and the retro Mido Cafe.
tips: Skewers, lamb or a seafood plate if you are still hungry after noodles.
Fortune tellers and opera singers usually appear later in the evening, so the end of this 7:30–8:20 PM walk is when they start to appear.
items.watch: Dai pai dong menus lean on seafood. Some stalls stay open past midnight depending on the day and weather.

items.title: Winter Wonderland in Tsim Sha Tsui
items.hours: 18 Nov 2026 – 5 Jan 2027, 7–11 PM daily. Dec 8 uses the normal schedule; late shows to 1 AM run only on 24–27 Dec and 1–2 Jan.
items.getThere: MTR to Tsim Sha Tsui or East Tsim Sha Tsui, then walk to the Hong Kong Cultural Centre precinct on the waterfront.
highlights: First edition of Prudential Hong Kong Winter Wonderland in TST: projection mapping, synchronised music and storytelling across the Cultural Centre, Museum of Art and Space Museum, themed as a northern-lights Christmas concert.
Best viewing: the Viewing Deck at the Hong Kong Cultural Centre, or outside the Museum of Art and Space Museum.
tips: The 8:30 PM visit sits well inside the 7–11 PM show hours.
WinterFest also has a 22 m tree and a 360° light-and-sound show at Statue Square Gardens, Central (same dates) if you want another evening.
items.watch: HKTB says the schedule can change without notice. Shows are partly suspended 28–30 Dec and fully on 31 Dec, which doesn't affect Dec 8.

items.title: Promenade, Dessert or an Arcade
items.hours: Silvercord Amusement & Games: 08:00–02:00. Retrocity Concept: 10:00–02:00. NAMCO branches close by 22:00–22:30 and none are in TST.
items.getThere: Silvercord Amusement & Games: Shop B03, Silvercord, 30 Canton Road, TST (tel 2730 3632). Retrocity Concept: LG23, Houston Centre, 63 Mody Road, TST (tel 6576 6680).
highlights: Silvercord: 16 linked Wangan Midnight Maximum Tune 5 / Initial D racing simulators, an original Taiko no Tatsujin, and Hatsune Miku rhythm games.
Retrocity Concept: a non-smoking retro arcade with classic video games, maimai DX, Drum Mania and Z Gundam, and retro games for sale.
tips: Silvercord on Canton Road is the closer arcade to the Cultural Centre waterfront.
If you are short on protein, pick something up at a 7-Eleven on the way back, as the day plan suggests.
items.watch: Arcade hours come from a 2024 guide and a directory that marks them 'pending verification'. Playspot lists Retrocity's building as Hoi Sun Centre; the street number is the same.
